Package com.framed.communicator.driver.protocol.mimic

Class MimicReplayProtocol

java.lang.Object
com.framed.core.Service
com.framed.io.protocol.Protocol
com.framed.communicator.driver.protocol.mimic.MimicReplayProtocol
public class MimicReplayProtocol extends Protocol
Replays a MIMIC-III Waveform Database record into the FRAMED EventBus in (scaled) real time, exercising the normal, non-interop data path: each decoded sample is published as a parsed DataPoint message on an address of the shape "<className>.<deviceID>.<channelID>.parsed", exactly as the live device drivers do. Downstream writers, dispatchers and CDSS reactors therefore see the record as if it came from a real monitor.

WFDB records are read directly (no external tooling): the master multi-segment header defines segment order and gaps, each segment header supplies the per-signal format, gain, baseline, units and name, and WfdbSegmentReader decodes the .dat payload. Gap ("~") and zero-length layout segments are skipped without stalling the replay clock, so the emitted stream is continuous. Signal names from the header become channel IDs (e.g. II, PLETH, ABP); values are converted to physical units, or passed through raw for uncalibrated signals.

Configuration keys

  • recordPath — path to the record's master .hea header file.
  • deviceID — device identifier stamped on every sample (sinks bind to this).
  • className — semantic category used as the address prefix (e.g. Waveform).
  • channels — JSON array of signal names to replay; empty replays all signals.
  • speed — replay-speed multiplier (1.0 = real time, 60 = 60×).
  • maxSeconds — stop after this much record time (0 = whole record).

Replay runs on a dedicated daemon-style thread started from connect(); the samples are paced against wall-clock time so trend/window reactors observe realistic timing. When the record is exhausted onReplayComplete() is invoked (by default it drains briefly and terminates the JVM, matching the CSV/JSONL replay driver).

Pacing statistics

Replay always accumulates cheap per-frame pacing statistics — how far each frame's actual emit time drifted from its scheduled time — and logs a one-line summary just before onReplayComplete(). The same figures are available programmatically via pacingStats(); together they answer whether the deployment sustains the record's sampling frequency. See MimicReplayProtocol.PacingStats for the threading contract.

  • Constructor Details

    • MimicReplayProtocol

      public MimicReplayProtocol(String id, EventBus eventBus, String recordPath, String deviceID, String className, org.json.JSONArray channels, double speed, double maxSeconds)
      Creates a MIMIC replay protocol. Parameter names match the JSON configuration keys resolved by Factory; the EventBus is injected automatically.
      Parameters:
      id - unique service identifier
      eventBus - the event bus samples are published on
      recordPath - path to the record's master .hea header file
      deviceID - device identifier stamped on every emitted sample
      className - semantic category used as the address prefix
      channels - signal names to replay; empty (or [ ]) replays every signal
      speed - replay-speed multiplier (1.0 = real time)
      maxSeconds - stop after this much record time in seconds; 0 replays the whole record

    • onReplayComplete

      protected void onReplayComplete()
      Invoked once the whole record (or maxSeconds of it) has been replayed. The default drains briefly to let downstream processing finish and then terminates the JVM, matching the CSV/JSONL replay driver's behaviour. Tests override this to avoid exiting.

    • pacingStats

      public MimicReplayProtocol.PacingStats pacingStats()
      Returns a snapshot of the replay's pacing fidelity — how well the producer held the configured sample rate.

      Threading: the underlying counters are written only by the replay thread. A caller on another thread sees a consistent, final snapshot once it has observed replay completion through a happens-before edge (e.g. a latch counted down from an overridden onReplayComplete()). Reading it during replay yields a torn but order-of-magnitude-correct view.

      Returns:
      the pacing statistics accumulated so far
